intro.heading: A problem-first analyst who works across the edges.
intro.body1: I am a data analyst and data scientist based in Adelaide, currently working at ASO7 level with the South Australia Police. Over the past four years my work has moved across climate risk modelling at CSIRO, ministerial dashboards for the South Australian Government, genomics pipelines at WEHI, and a mental health app at the University of Melbourne. Generalist by nature, specialist by discipline.
intro.body2: The thread through all of it is the same. I start from the decision that needs making and the smallest amount of data needed to make it well, then reach for the right tool rather than the fashionable one. Problem first, not model first. That habit is what lets the same person be useful in a research lab, a government intelligence team, and an engineering project.

hardware.desc: Primary machine. The M4 chip handles PyTorch training, Docker containers, and 47 browser tabs simultaneously.
One wide monitor. No more alt-tabbing between terminals and notebooks.
Tactile switches. The clickety-clack is 40% of the productivity.
Active noise cancellation — the second-best productivity tool after good coffee.

editorTerminal.desc: VS Code with AI superpowers. This entire website was built in it.
With zsh and Oh My Zsh. Theme: minimal. Plugins: git, z, syntax highlighting.
Terminal multiplexer. Keeps sessions alive when I inevitably close the wrong window.

languages.desc: Primary language. NumPy, Pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch, FastAPI — the whole ecosystem.
For anything web-facing. Types save future-me from past-me.
PostgreSQL day-to-day. BigQuery for large-scale. Still the most underrated skill in data science.
For statistical analysis and publication-quality visualisations. ggplot2 is genuinely beautiful.
Automating everything that shouldn't need automating but somehow does.

dataMl.desc: Deep learning framework of choice. Dynamic graphs, Pythonic, excellent ecosystem.
Still the gold standard for classical ML. Pipelines are underused.
SQL transformation layer. Version-controlled data models — finally.
For exploration and sharing analysis. VS Code notebooks for production.
Dashboards for non-technical stakeholders. Sometimes the right tool is the accessible one.

webDev.desc: Framework of choice for web. Pages Router on React 19 — fast, file-based, fantastic DX.
Utility-first styling. Initially sceptical. Now converted.
Deploy → done. Preview URLs on every push. The best CI/CD experience I've used.
Design and prototyping. Also for communicating with designers who don't speak code.

productivity.desc: Project notes, research logs, and second brain. Imperfect but flexible.
Issue tracking for Mapiva. Fast, minimal, opinionated — very Nothing OS.
Window management on macOS. Free. Simple. Indispensable.

infoAccessibility.metaDescription: How rin.contact handles accessibility — contrast, focus, screen readers, motion, and keyboard navigation.
infoAccessibility.ogSubtitle: How rin.contact handles accessibility — contrast, focus...
infoAccessibility.heading: Accessibility at rin.contact
infoAccessibility.intro: This site aims to be usable by everyone. Here's what we do — and what we're still improving.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.prefix: If you encounter a barrier, please reach out.
feedback.suffix: — I take accessibility seriously and will do my best to fix issues.

items.label: Contrast ratios
items.detail: Text meets WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text). Black on white, dark grey on light grey — tested with WebAIM Contrast Checker.

items.label: Colour independence
items.detail: Information is never conveyed by colour alone. Icons, labels, and text accompany all interactive states.

items.label: Nothing OS palette
items.detail: Monochromatic design reduces reliance on colour perception. Accent red (#FF3C3C) used sparingly for emphasis.

items.label: Focus indicators
items.detail: All interactive elements have a visible :focus-visible outline (2px solid black). Mouse/tap focus is suppressed to avoid clutter; keyboard focus is always shown.

items.label: Tab order
items.detail: Logical tab sequence follows visual layout. Skip links available where structure benefits (e.g. long pages).

items.label: Escape & Enter
items.detail: Modals and overlays can be closed with Escape. Buttons and links activate with Enter/Space.

items.label: Semantic HTML
items.detail: Headings (h1–h6), landmarks (main, nav, section), and ARIA roles used where appropriate. Form labels associated with inputs.

items.label: Alt text
items.detail: Images have descriptive alt attributes. Decorative images use aria-hidden or empty alt.

items.label: Live regions
items.detail: Dynamic content (toasts, form status) uses aria-live for announcements without disrupting reading flow.

items.label: prefers-reduced-motion
items.detail: Respecting the user's system preference. Where implemented, animations are disabled or simplified when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is set.

items.label: Animation duration
items.detail: Transitions kept to 150–300ms. No auto-playing videos or infinite loops that can't be paused.

items.label: Contact form
items.detail: Labels, error messages, and success feedback. Required fields marked. Validation before submit.

items.label: Touch targets
items.detail: Buttons and links sized to at least 44×44px where possible for touch devices.

items.label: Easter eggs
items.detail: Some hidden features (Konami code, secret word) are discoverable but not announced. They don't block core tasks.

items.label: Canvas content
items.detail: Snake game, Matrix rain, and generative art use canvas — not natively accessible. Text alternatives or descriptions provided where feasible.

items.label: Third-party
items.detail: External embeds (e.g. QR codes, wttr.in) follow their own accessibility. We can't control them.

infoManifest.metaDescription: What I believe about data, work, and building things.
infoManifest.ogSubtitle: What I believe about data, work, and building things.
infoManifest.heading: Manifest
infoManifest.intro: What I believe about data, work, and building things.
principles: Every decision is intentional. If it doesn't earn its place, it doesn't ship.
Empty space is part of the design. Density ≠ quality.
Mobile-first, always. 375px is the source of truth.
No gradients, no drop-shadows. Flat monochrome.
Accessibility is not optional. AA contrast, focus rings, descriptive alt text.
Ship it, then improve it. Version numbers and counting.
